title: Choose the visual world for the Propulsor shell
question: The roll assigned Design Criteria Monograph. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Design Criteria Monograph
options.lineage: Mid-century aerospace design-criteria monographs and technical reports
options.thesis: The engine reads like the monograph written about it: numbered sections, a nomenclature table, every figure captioned, every number cited to its tier.
options.viewport: Buff contents rail with decimal sections (1 Requirements to 7 Verification) and a live engine profile; a running head of section number, title, design and rev; a Nomenclature panel of symbols, values and [L1] citations on the right.
options.risk: Reads as a document rather than a tool if the numbering is set too large, and tips into nostalgia if the ground drifts cream.

raised.raise: States are printed marks: zero radius, one-device-pixel rules, focus bracketed, disabled struck through.
Density courage: results set as tight tabular columns; the Dashboard's KPI tiles become a nomenclature table.
One grotesque carries heading, label and caption; the only second voice is math italic for symbols.
Colour roles are exclusive: buff marks structure only, spot blue marks only where you are and what has focus.
Map and index are one space: the contents rail carries the live engine contour, lit where the current section lives.

options.label: Drawing Sheet
options.lineage: ASME Y14 / ISO 7200 engineering drawing sheets
options.thesis: The shell is a drawing set: a title block holds the design's identity, a revision block holds its history, and changes since the last solve are redlined.
options.viewport: Sheet index along the top edge, the work area as the drawing field, a title block bottom-right carrying design, rev, propellant, thrust and Pc, and a revision block listing the last edits.
options.risk: The most familiar engineering costume there is; the title block and border cost width at the 900 px minimum window.

options.label: Boarding Pass & Gate Board
options.lineage: Airline boarding passes and live departure boards
options.thesis: A re-solve is a gate change: the row moves, and a changed value stays lit until you have noticed it.
options.viewport: Status strip as a segmented pass (design, rev, propellant, F, Pc, O/F); issues as a departures board that reranks by severity; edited results stay amber until acknowledged.
options.case: Holds product clarity: 'changed stays lit until noticed' is the clearest answer to live re-solve. Loses audience identification: engineers don't see their work in travel ephemera.
options.risk: Becomes a travel-app costume if the pass segments leak beyond the status strip.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: Every junction shows only the choices ahead.
options.viewport: Yellow bands naming the next step at each tier.
options.case: Loses both: no audience link, and the world may not supply navigation on a working screen.

options.label: Centre-Rail Reference Setting
options.thesis: Inputs and results twinned around a rail of provenance keys.
options.viewport: Two narrow columns around a tier-key rail.
options.case: Loses both: scholarly editions are foreign to engineers, and the form dictates layout.

options.label: Hall Catalog
options.thesis: Every subsystem a stamp-sized cell keyed to a map.
options.viewport: Subsystem thumbnails keyed to an engine map.
options.case: Loses both: fan-culture ephemera, and cells hide numbers.
options.kept: Map and index are one space.

options.label: Annual Plate Section
options.viewport: Figures as registered plates with crosshairs.
options.case: Loses both: a design-world artifact, decorative furniture over data.
options.risk: Gallery mood on an engineering tool.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: Pure black and white numeric density.
options.case: Loses both: no colour means no fail/warn state, and strobing harms long sessions.

canonCard.label: Engineering workbench, played straight
canonCard.thesis: What engineering desktop tools ship: model tree, ribbon, property grid, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Ribbon of grouped commands, model tree on the left, tabbed work area, property grid on the right.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every CAE tool by design.
